Explored three tables (customers, products, orders) in SQLite, calculated Recency, Frequency and Monetary values for each customer, and scored them to build five segments. Customers inactive for 90–179 days are labelled At Risk and 180+ days Lost, unless they already qualify as High Value or Loyal. The results were brought into Excel to build the dashboard.

SEGMENTCUSTOMERSREVENUE
High Value176₹16,909,608
Loyal110₹4,706,097
At Risk220₹7,191,609
Lost468₹16,661,255
Regular25₹1,706,457
The dataset is synthetic, and "churn risk" here means 90+ days without a purchase — a project-defined inactivity indicator, not confirmed churn. Figures illustrate the method rather than a real company's results.

Key findings

  • Value is concentrated: High Value (176 customers) and Lost (468 customers) segments each bring roughly 35% of historical revenue — together about 71%.
  • Re-engagement opportunity: the Lost segment alone represents about ₹16.7M of past revenue, worth testing targeted win-back campaigns.
  • Retention gap: 901 of 999 customers (90.19%) have been inactive for 90+ days.

Retail Sales & Profit Intelligence

2026 · Completed

Built on the Brazilian Olist E-Commerce dataset. Raw CSVs were cleaned and merged in Python/Pandas into a star schema (a central sales fact table with date, product, customer, and seller dimensions), then key metrics were recalculated independently in SQLite to cross-check the Python results before building the Power BI dashboard.

*Olist has no product-cost data, so profit comes from a simulated cost model (category cost ratios of roughly 60–75% of price, plus transaction-level variation). Profit and margin figures illustrate the method — they are estimates, not real company earnings.

Key findings

  • Revenue is concentrated: São Paulo brings about 38% of revenue (R$5.2M), and SP, RJ and MG together about 63%.
  • Retention is the biggest gap: only about 3.1% of customers buy more than once.
  • Credit cards dominate: 79.7% of revenue, averaging 3.6 instalments per order versus about 1 for other methods.
  • Volume ≠ order value: SP has the lowest average order value among the top 10 states (R$125.75, against R$152.28 in Bahia).
  • Delivery is strong overall (93.4% on time), but a few northern and north-eastern states such as AL, MA and SE show much higher late-delivery rates.
